records.text: White has a new passed pawn! No enemy pawn ahead on its file or the files beside it. A very important pawn development, if I may say so.
Black has a new passed pawn! No enemy pawn ahead on its file or the files beside it. A very important pawn development, if I may say so.
Another move would have made a passed pawn for White! I notice these things. Promotion would still need work.
Another move would have made a passed pawn for Black! I notice these things. Promotion would still need work.
White has an isolated pawn now. No friendly pawn on either neighboring file. Pawn support is a job the pieces may have to cover.
Black has an isolated pawn now. No friendly pawn on either neighboring file. Pawn support is a job the pieces may have to cover.
The alternative would have left White an isolated pawn. No friendly pawn on the files next door; that's a real change in the support team.
The alternative would have left Black an isolated pawn. No friendly pawn on the files next door; that's a real change in the support team.
White has doubled pawns now, sharing a file. Pawns do notice the seating arrangements.
Black has doubled pawns now, sharing a file. Pawns do notice the seating arrangements.
Another move would have doubled White's pawns. More of the pawn team on the same file; not automatically a disaster.
Another move would have doubled Black's pawns. More of the pawn team on the same file; not automatically a disaster.
White's rook has an open file! No pawns from either side occupy it. The rook's next job still depends on the other pieces.
Black's rook has an open file! No pawns from either side occupy it. The rook's next job still depends on the other pieces.
The alternative would have given White's rook an open file. No pawns there, though pieces could still be in the way.
The alternative would have given Black's rook an open file. No pawns there, though pieces could still be in the way.
White's rook has a half-open file now. No White pawns on it, but Black pawns remain. The word half matters!
Black's rook has a half-open file now. No Black pawns on it, but White pawns remain. The word half matters!
Another move would have given White's rook a half-open file: no White pawns there, with Black pawns still present. A different working arrangement.
Another move would have given Black's rook a half-open file: no Black pawns there, with White pawns still present. A different working arrangement.
White's knight has a defender now! Somebody has taken on a job that wasn't being done.
Black's knight has a defender now! Somebody has taken on a job that wasn't being done.
White's bishop was unguarded. Now it has a defender. That's teamwork taking shape.
Black's bishop was unguarded. Now it has a defender. That's teamwork taking shape.
A guard for White's rook! It had no defender before this move. Support counts, even for the big pieces.
A guard for Black's rook! It had no defender before this move. Support counts, even for the big pieces.
White's queen has gained a defender. Even the queen can use someone covering that job!
Black's queen has gained a defender. Even the queen can use someone covering that job!
Another move would have given White's knight a defender. That support job was going unfilled.
Another move would have given Black's knight a defender. That support job was going unfilled.
The alternative would have supplied the guard White's bishop lacked. Someone would have been covering it.
The alternative would have supplied the guard Black's bishop lacked. Someone would have been covering it.
A different move would have given White's rook a defender where it had none. Rooks need support too!
A different move would have given Black's rook a defender where it had none. Rooks need support too!
White's queen would have gained a defender after another move. That is a job worth noticing, even for a queen.
Black's queen would have gained a defender after another move. That is a job worth noticing, even for a queen.
White's knight has no defender now. The last guard is gone; that support job is empty.
Black's knight has no defender now. The last guard is gone; that support job is empty.
White's bishop has lost its last defender. Nobody is covering it now, though that doesn't prove it can be taken.
Black's bishop has lost its last defender. Nobody is covering it now, though that doesn't prove it can be taken.
White's rook has lost all its protection. Big piece, empty support team. That alone doesn't make it lost.
Black's rook has lost all its protection. Big piece, empty support team. That alone doesn't make it lost.
White's queen is without a defender now. Royal importance doesn't fill a vacant support job!
Black's queen is without a defender now. Royal importance doesn't fill a vacant support job!
The alternative would have left White's knight without its last defender. That support job would be empty.
The alternative would have left Black's knight without its last defender. That support job would be empty.
Another move would have left White's bishop undefended. Nobody covering it, though not necessarily a capture that works.
Another move would have left Black's bishop undefended. Nobody covering it, though not necessarily a capture that works.
White's rook would have lost its last guard after a different move. Even a rook can't appoint its own defender!
Black's rook would have lost its last guard after a different move. Even a rook can't appoint its own defender!
A different move would have left White's queen without a guard. The queen's job and the defender's job aren't the same thing.
A different move would have left Black's queen without a guard. The queen's job and the defender's job aren't the same thing.
A knight takes its first step off the starting square! Development is officially under way for that piece.
The knight is out of its original square for the first time. I like to keep track of who's left home.
First outing for the knight! It has made the move off its starting square.
That knight had not moved from home before. Now it has. A development milestone worth noticing!
Look at that, the bishop's first move! Off its starting square and ready for its job.
A bishop leaves home for the first time. Diagonals are its whole job, and now it can start.
Off its starting square for the first time, the bishop joins the team. Every piece needs a role!
That bishop had been sitting at home. Now it's out and has a job to find!
Another move would have brought a knight off its starting square for the first time. Its first outing was available!
The alternative would have started a knight's development. Still at home until then, waiting for its first move.
A different move would have been that knight's first trip from its original square. That belongs in the comparison!
Another choice would have moved a knight away from home for the first time. That was a job waiting to be done!
The better move would have sent a bishop out for its first job. Worth noting!
A bishop was still waiting at home. The better move would have given it work to do.
With the better move, a bishop would have left its starting square for the first time. Development matters to the whole team!
Had the better move been played, a bishop would have stepped out of its home square for the first time. One more piece would have had a role to fill!
This gives away some of what the position offered. The better move would have kept more of it.
There was a better choice, and this move pays a price for passing it up. It needn't be a missing piece to count.
The position deserved a stronger move than this. Compare the alternative and what it leaves on the board.
This choice leaves less than the best move would. Give that better option a proper inspection!
The other side can capture immediately! Put that reply on the list before anything else.
There is a capture ready in reply. What gets taken matters; whether the trade pays is another question.
Something can be taken on the very next move. That deserves immediate attention!
The reply has a capture available already. No preparation needed to make that capture.
You made their last mistake matter! An opportunity with a job to do, and you put it to work.
They slipped on the previous move. You used the chance instead of letting it sit there. Excellent attention!
Your move takes advantage of their last error. That's an opportunity properly handled!
A different move would have done the job better. Give that option a proper look.
The stronger move is worth trying on the board. Compare what each choice leaves behind.
Another move was better here. I wouldn't leave that part of the explanation out!
The passed pawn has advanced! Closer to promotion, still with work ahead. I'm following this very closely.
An existing passer takes another step toward promotion. Progress in a pawn's career! Getting there is still another matter.
The strongest reply gives check. An attack on the king goes straight to the top of the jobs list!
Check is the best reply here. If played, it would make the king's safety the immediate job.
Exactly the intended lesson move! Consider that task done.
You found the move this lesson wanted. Nicely handled!
Yes, that matches the lesson. Ready for the next bit!
Correct move! Keep concentrating; this puzzle still has work for us.
That part is right! The puzzle isn't finished, so stay on the job.
You've got this move. Now for the next part of the puzzle!
That's the move in the opening line you're practicing! Nicely remembered.
Correct recall! It matches your repertoire, just as required.
Yes, your answer fits the studied opening line. A detail remembered properly!
Best! The strongest move in the position deserves a proper nod.
Exactly the best choice here! That earns my most serious approval.
A good move! Sound work, although a better choice was available.
Good, not best. This move holds up, and I take sound work seriously!
